Subject: Sublicense and retrain carveouts - MSA & Order Form redlines

Hi Marissa / Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we’re excited to move forward. Our legal team has redlined the MSA and Order Form with two principal asks: (1) a narrow right to sublicense Generated Output to our end customers so they can use features in our product (we're not asking for broad transfer of title, just necessary sublicensing to deliver functionality), and (2) an explicit prohibition on Redwood using Generated Output to train or finetune models unless Greenline provides an explicit opt-in.

Attached are the redlines with comments. Can Redwood confirm whether those carveouts are acceptable or, if not, what compromise language you’d propose? Also flagging that our procurement team needs a short turnaround.

Appreciate it —
Emily Park
Head of Legal Operations, Greenline AI

Subject: Re: Sublicense and retrain carveouts - MSA & Order Form redlines

Hi Emily / Alex — thanks for sending the redlines and context. We’re very eager to close GLN but want to be careful about precedent on training and on any transfer-like rights. High level:

- Generated Output: Redwood’s standard position is to grant customers a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use Generated Output for their business purposes. We don’t typically assign title.
- Sublicense: We can consider a limited sublicense carveout that allows Customer to enable end-user functionality (i.e., to provide the product to their customers) but not broad downstream transfer or resale. We’d want language that ties the sublicense strictly to delivering the Customer’s product features and prevents re-granting to third parties unrelated to product delivery.
- Training: Redwood will not use Customer Generated Output to train or finetune models without explicit, documented opt-in in the Order Form (or a separate agreement). Our product telemetry / aggregated usage signals may be used for internal product improvements but we can narrow that to anonymized/aggregated signals, not raw outputs or customer content.

I’ve attached a draft redline that captures the above (see greenline_redlined_msa_v1.pdf). Internal legal needs to confirm exact language — looping Laura to propose alternative clause text. If we can get to a compromise on the sublicense scope and a clear opt-in for retrain, I think we can move quickly.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sublicense and retrain carveouts - MSA & Order Form redlines

Marissa / team — quick legal take. Proposed compromise language below (we should include in both MSA and Order Form and mark the Order Form as the source of any opt-in to training):

1) Customer Generated Output. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Generated Output. Redwood grants Customer a worldwide, non-exclusive, sublicensable (solely to the extent necessary to provide Customer’s product or services to its end users), perpetual license to use, reproduce, and display Generated Output. Any sublicense must be limited in scope and cannot permit third parties to use Generated Output to train, fine-tune, or develop models.

2) Model Training; Opt-In. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Generated Output to train, fine-tune or otherwise improve models unless Customer provides explicit written consent in the Order Form ("Training Opt-In"). If Customer opts in, Redwood will only use the specified datasets and will provide a summary of types of usage; Customer may revoke opt-in with 60 days’ notice.

3) Telemetry and Aggregated Improvements. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage statistics for product improvements and safety monitoring, provided such data cannot reasonably be used to reconstruct Customer Content or Generated Output.

If Sales agrees to the limited sublicense carveout above (narrowly tailored), Legal is comfortable with that path. If Sales prefers to permit broader sublicensing for certain partners, we need a separate partner-specific addendum and a higher-tier approval.

Please advise if you want me to prepare the exact MSA/Order Form redline for signature.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sublicense and retrain carveouts - MSA & Order Form redlines

Hi Emily / Alex — thanks for your patience. Internal legal proposed the compromise language below and we’d like to confirm if this covers Greenline’s needs:

--- Proposed summary for the redline ---
1) Customer retains ownership of Generated Output. Redwood grants Customer a limited right to sublicense Generated Output solely to enable Customer to provide Product functionality to its end users; sublicenses cannot be used to train models or to broadly transfer ownership.
2) Training explicit opt-in in Order Form. Redwood will not use Generated Output to train or finetune models without a written opt-in in the Order Form. If Greenline opts in, the scope, retention, and revocation process will be documented.
3) Redwood may use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for product improvements (no raw outputs).

I’ve attached the redlined MSA and Order Form with the clause tracked. If that sounds good, let us know and we’ll produce final clean copies for signature. If you’d like any tweaks (e.g., stricter revocation timing or audit rights), flag those and we’ll route to Legal for a quick review.

Best,
